yes_case.case: The closest historical episodes are the original negotiation and finalization of the 1996 Ganga Water Treaty under Prime Minister H.D. Deve Gowda and Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina, and the historic 2015 Land Boundary Agreement (LBA) signed by Prime Minister Narendra Modi and Prime Minister Sheikh Hasina. This episode differs from the 1996 episode in that the political leadership in Bangladesh has recently shifted away from the Awami League, introducing a temporary interim administration; however, it differs from ordinary stalled bilateral disputes because both nations share an absolute, existential dependency on the Ganga basin's dry-season flow, mirroring the deep-seated urgency that ultimately compelled the 2015 LBA ratification despite decades of domestic political friction in India. Furthermore, unlike past disputes where water sharing was held hostage by broader security friction, the modern strategic imperative to maintain a stable, cooperative eastern border forces both Delhi and Dhaka to prioritize finalizing technical framework renewals to prevent diplomatic vacuums, just as they did when overcoming domestic resistance to operationalize the 1974 Land Boundary Agreement decades later.
